apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: akili
  displayName: Akili
  version: 1.3.0
  description: Security-first control plane for autonomous AI operator agents. Default deny, explicit allow, always auditable.
  category: DevOps
  icon: https://github.com/goakili.png
  homepage: https://github.com/goakili/akili
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    email: me@jkaninda.dev
    website: https://jkaninda.dev
  tags: [ai, agents, operations, automation, devops, llm]
  minMiabi: "1.10.10" # routes

inputs:
  - key: public_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The HTTPS URL Akili is served on. Agents connect to it, and it is used in install commands and links.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https://"
    placeholder: https://akili.example.com
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: Email of the first owner account, created on the first start.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password of the first owner account. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 20
  - key: jwt_secret
    label: JWT secret
    help: Signs session and API tokens (at least 32 characters). Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 48
  - key: encryption_key
    label: Encryption key
    help: Encrypts provider keys, integration tokens and the policy-signing key at rest (at least 32 characters). Keep it; without it stored secrets cannot be read. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 48
  - key: anthropic_api_key
    label: Anthropic API key
    help: Optional. Seeds Claude as the default model provider on the first start. Without it, Akili starts with a scripted test provider; add a real one under Settings → Model providers.
    type: password
  - key: license
    label: Enterprise license
    help: Optional. An Akili Enterprise license token (akili-v1.…). Licenses are bound to this deployment's Install ID, shown under Settings → License after install; you can also install the license there later.
    type: password
  - key: trusted_proxies
    label: Trusted proxies
    help: CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For header is trusted, so rate limits and the audit log see real client IPs. The default covers Miabi's gateway on a private network.
    type: string
    default: 10.62.0.0/16

databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto
  - name: redis
    engine: redis
    version: "8-alpine"
    placement: dedicated

applications:
  - name: akili
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/akili
    tag: "0.4.0"
    ports:
      - container: 9000
        scheme: http
    env:
      AKILI_ENV: production
      AKILI_PORT: "9000"
      AKILI_PUBLIC_URL: "{{ .inputs.public_url }}"
      AKILI_COOKIE_SECURE: "true"
      AKILI_TRUSTED_PROXIES: "{{ .inputs.trusted_proxies }}"
      AKILI_DATABASE_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}?sslmode=disable"
      AKILI_REDIS_URL: "{{ .databases.redis.uri }}"
      AKILI_JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
      AKILI_ENCRYPTION_KEY: "{{ .inputs.encryption_key }}"
      AKILI_ADMIN_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      AKILI_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "{{ .inputs.anthropic_api_key }}"
      AKILI_LICENSE: "{{ .inputs.license }}"
      AKILI_LOG_LEVEL: info
    secretEnv:
      # Both URLs embed their password, so they are stored encrypted like one.
      - AKILI_DATABASE_URL
      - AKILI_REDIS_URL
      - AKILI_JWT_SECRET
      - AKILI_ENCRYPTION_KEY
      - AKILI_ADMIN_PASSWORD
      - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
      - AKILI_LICENSE
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /healthz
      port: 9000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 15

# Created on install when the URL's domain belongs to this workspace; skipped with a warning otherwise.
routes:
  - app: akili
    host: "{{ .inputs.public_url }}"

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: akili-agent
  displayName: Akili Agent
  version: 1.3.0
  description: Security-first autonomous AI operator agent. Dials out to an Akili control plane; every action is policy-checked, approved and audited there.
  category: DevOps
  icon: https://github.com/goakili.png
  homepage: https://github.com/goakili/akili
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    email: me@jkaninda.dev
    website: https://jkaninda.dev
  tags: [ai, agent, operations, automation, devops]
inputs:
  - key: akili_url
    label: Control plane URL
    help: The public URL of your Akili control plane, e.g. https://akili.example.com.
    type: string
    required: true
    placeholder: https://akili.example.com
  - key: join_token
    label: Join token
    help: The one-time join token shown when you create the agent in Akili (Agents → Add agent). It is used once to enroll; the agent then keeps its own key in the volume.
    type: password
    required: true
  - key: ca_cert
    label: Control plane CA (base64)
    help: Only for a control plane with a self-signed or private-CA certificate. The CA certificate as PEM, or base64-encoded PEM, e.g. the output of `base64 < ca.pem | tr -d '\n'`.
    type: string
volumes:
  - name: state
applications:
  - name: akili-agent
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/akili-agent
    tag: "0.4.0"
    env:
      AKILI_URL: "{{ .inputs.akili_url }}"
      AKILI_JOIN_TOKEN: "{{ .inputs.join_token }}"
      AKILI_STATE_DIR: /var/lib/akili-agent
      AKILI_LOG_FORMAT: json
      AKILI_CA_CERT_PEM: "{{ .inputs.ca_cert }}"
    secretEnv:
      - AKILI_JOIN_TOKEN
    mounts:
      - volume: state
        path: /var/lib/akili-agent

    required: true
    placeholder: http://mb-app-mysite:8080
  - key: difficulty
    label: Challenge difficulty
    help: Leading zeroes the client must find. 4 is the default; raise it only if scrapers are getting through, since every visitor pays the cost.
    type: number
    default: "4"
    required: true
    pattern: '^([1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])$'
  - key: serve_robots_txt
    label: Serve robots.txt
    help: Let Anubis answer /robots.txt with a policy asking well-behaved crawlers to stay away.
    type: bool
    default: "true"
  - key: og_passthrough
    label: Pass through Open Graph tags
    help: Fetch the upstream's Open Graph tags so link previews keep working for challenged visitors.
    type: bool
    default: "true"

configs:
  # Shipped as a config so editing it under Configs redeploys Anubis with the new rules.
  - name: policy
    mode: "0644"
    files:
      botPolicy.yaml: |
        bots:
          - name: cloudflare-workers
            headers_regex:
              CF-Worker: .*
            action: DENY

          - name: well-known
            path_regex: ^/.well-known/.*$
            action: ALLOW
          - name: favicon
            path_regex: ^/favicon.ico$
            action: ALLOW
          - name: robots-txt
            path_regex: ^/robots.txt$
            action: ALLOW

          # A request matching no rule is allowed, so add ALLOW rules for feed readers and monitoring.
          - name: generic-browser
            user_agent_regex: Mozilla
            action: CHALLENGE

  - name: anubis
    primary: true
    image: ghcr.io/techarohq/anubis
    tag: "v1.28.2"
    ports:

        scheme: http

      TARGET: "{{ .inputs.target }}"
      DIFFICULTY: "{{ .inputs.difficulty }}"
      SERVE_ROBOTS_TXT: "{{ .inputs.serve_robots_txt }}"
      OG_PASSTHROUGH: "{{ .inputs.og_passthrough }}"
      OG_EXPIRY_TIME: "24h"
      POLICY_FNAME: /data/cfg/botPolicy.yaml
    mounts:
      - config: policy
        key: botPolicy.yaml
        path: /data/cfg/botPolicy.yaml
    healthcheck:

      command: anubis --healthcheck
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: certio
  displayName: Certio
  version: 1.3.0
  description: Self-signed PKI and TLS certificate management — issue, renew, revoke and distribute internal certificates, with ACME and a CRL/OCSP responder.
  category: Security
  icon: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jkaninda/certio/main/branding/logo.svg
  homepage: https://github.com/jkaninda/certio
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    email: me@jkaninda.dev
    website: https://jkaninda.dev
  tags: [pki, tls, certificates, ca, acme, security, self-hosted]
  minMiabi: "1.10.10" # routes

inputs:
  - key: base_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The URL Certio is served on. It is baked into the CRL distribution point of every certificate issued from here, so it must be the URL clients can actually reach — changing it later does not fix certificates already issued.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://certio.example.com
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: The first administrator, created once on an empty database.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the initial administrator. Leave blank to auto-generate, then change it after signing in.
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 20
  - key: master_key
    label: Master key
    help: "Encrypts every stored private key (AES-256-GCM). Leave blank to auto-generate — then copy it out and back it up somewhere other than this server: lose it, or change it, and every certificate's private key is unreadable. A pasted key must be 64 hex characters, base64 of 32 bytes, or exactly 32 characters."
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    # Certio needs a 32-byte key; Miabi generates exactly `length` alphanumerics, so only 32 parses at boot.
    length: 32
    pattern: "^([0-9a-fA-F]{64}|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{42,43}={0,2}|.{32})$"
  - key: jwt_secret
    label: JWT secret
    help: Signs dashboard sessions. Leave blank to auto-generate; rotating it only signs everyone out.
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 32
  - key: organization
    label: Organization
    help: Default Organization (O) on issued certificates.
    type: string
    default: Example Ltd
  - key: country
    label: Country code
    help: Default two-letter country (C) on issued certificates.
    type: string
    default: US
    pattern: "^[A-Za-z]{2}$"

# No volume: with Postgres, Certio keeps no state on its own filesystem.
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto

applications:
  - name: certio
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/certio
    tag: "0.2.1"
    ports:
      - container: 8080
        scheme: http
    env:
      # Refuses to boot without a real master key and JWT secret, and marks session cookies secure.
      CERTIO_PRODUCTION: "true"
      CERTIO_BASE_URL: "{{ .inputs.base_url }}"

      CERTIO_DB_DRIVER: postgres
      CERTIO_DB_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}"

      CERTIO_MASTER_KEY: "{{ .inputs.master_key }}"
      CERTIO_JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
      CERTIO_ADMIN_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      CERTIO_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      CERTIO_DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION: "{{ .inputs.organization }}"
      CERTIO_DEFAULT_COUNTRY: "{{ .inputs.country }}"

      # once lets the issuer collect the private key, then closes the door.
      CERTIO_KEY_DOWNLOAD_POLICY: once

      # Renewal and expiry warnings run in-process.
      CERTIO_SCHEDULER_ENABLED: "true"
      CERTIO_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL: 1h
      CERTIO_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS: "30"

      CERTIO_LOG_LEVEL: info
      CERTIO_LOG_FORMAT: json
    secretEnv:
      - CERTIO_MASTER_KEY
      - CERTIO_JWT_SECRET
      - CERTIO_ADMIN_PASSWORD
      - CERTIO_DB_URL
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /health
      port: 8080
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10
# Created on install when the URL's domain belongs to this workspace; skipped with a warning otherwise.
routes:
  - app: certio
    host: "{{ .inputs.base_url }}"

    required: true
    generate: true

    type: string

  - key: country

      CERTIO_BASE_URL: "{{ .inputs.base_url }}"

    healthcheck:

kind: Template
metadata:

  displayName: Dragonfly
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Redis- and Memcached-compatible in-memory datastore built for multi-core machines, with snapshots to disk.
  category: Database
  icon: https://github.com/dragonflydb.png
  homepage: https://www.dragonflydb.io
  tags: [cache, key-value, redis, memcached, in-memory]

inputs:
  - key: password
    label: Password
    help: Required for AUTH. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
    required: true
  - key: maxmemory
    label: Max memory
    help: Upper bound on memory used by the datastore, e.g. 512mb or 2gb. Leave at 0 to let Dragonfly size itself against the container's limit.
    type: string
    default: "0"
    required: true
    pattern: '^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4}(kb|mb|gb))$'
  - key: cache_mode
    label: Cache mode
    help: Evict the least valuable keys when memory runs out instead of refusing writes. Turn this off when the data must not disappear.
    type: bool
    default: "false"
  - key: snapshot_cron
    label: Snapshot schedule
    help: Cron expression for automatic snapshots to the data volume, e.g. "0 * * * *" for hourly. Leave blank to snapshot only on shutdown.
    type: string
    default: "0 * * * *"
    placeholder: 0 * * * *

volumes:
  - name: data    # /data — snapshots (dump.rdb)

applications:
  - name: dragonfly
    primary: true
    image: docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly
    tag: "v1.40.2"
    # No ports: the gateway cannot route Redis protocol; flags go through sh so the password stays out of argv.
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - >-
        exec dragonfly --logtostderr --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 6379
        --requirepass "$DF_PASSWORD" --maxmemory "$DF_MAXMEMORY"
        --cache_mode="$DF_CACHE_MODE" --dir /data
        ${DF_SNAPSHOT_CRON:+--snapshot_cron="$DF_SNAPSHOT_CRON"}
    env:
      DF_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.password }}"
      DF_MAXMEMORY: "{{ .inputs.maxmemory }}"
      DF_CACHE_MODE: "{{ .inputs.cache_mode }}"
      DF_SNAPSHOT_CRON: "{{ .inputs.snapshot_cron }}"
    secretEnv:
      - DF_PASSWORD
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: command
      command: echo PING | nc -q1 localhost 6379
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 15

  tags: [git, vcs, devops, ci-cd, code-review, issues]

inputs:

    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL GitLab is served on. It ends up in clone URLs, emails and every redirect, so set it to the domain you will attach in Miabi.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://gitlab.example.com
  - key: root_password
    label: Root password
    help: Initial password for the built-in `root` account, applied on first boot only. Leave blank to auto-generate; change it after signing in.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
  - key: time_zone
    label: Time zone
    help: IANA time zone used for timestamps and scheduled pipelines.
    type: string
    default: UTC
    placeholder: Europe/Brussels

volumes:
  - name: config    # /etc/gitlab      — secrets, generated certificates

  - name: data      # /var/opt/gitlab  — repositories, uploads, the bundled database

  - name: omnibus
    # Carries the initial root password: keep it out of apply plans and behind an audited reveal.
    sensitive: true
    mode: "0600"
    files:
      gitlab.rb: |
        external_url '{{ .inputs.external_url }}'
        gitlab_rails['time_zone'] = '{{ .inputs.time_zone }}'
        gitlab_rails['initial_root_password'] = '{{ .inputs.root_password }}'

        # An https external_url would make omnibus listen on 443 and try to issue its own certificate, which fails here.
        nginx['listen_port'] = 80
        nginx['listen_https'] = false
        letsencrypt['enable'] = false
        nginx['proxy_set_headers'] = {
          'X-Forwarded-Proto' => 'https',
          'X-Forwarded-Ssl' => 'on'
        }

        # SSH is not published (see README), so do not advertise an unreachable port.
        gitlab_rails['gitlab_shell_ssh_port'] = 22

        puma['worker_processes'] = 2
        sidekiq['max_concurrency'] = 10
        prometheus_monitoring['enable'] = false

  - name: gitlab
    primary: true
    image: gitlab/gitlab-ce
    tag: "19.5.3-ce.0"
    ports:
      # TLS terminates at Miabi's gateway, so the container only ever speaks HTTP.
      - container: 80
        scheme: http
    env:
      TZ: "{{ .inputs.time_zone }}"
    mounts:
      - volume: config
        path: /etc/gitlab
      - volume: logs
        path: /var/log/gitlab
      - volume: data
        path: /var/opt/gitlab

        key: gitlab.rb
        path: /etc/gitlab/gitlab.rb
        mode: "0600"
    healthcheck:
      # First boot runs reconfigure + migrations (5-10 minutes), so a shorter start period would kill it mid-install.
      type: http
      path: /-/health
      port: 80
      intervalSeconds: 60
      timeoutSeconds: 15
      retries: 5
      startPeriodSeconds: 600
# Created on install when the URL's domain belongs to this workspace; skipped with a warning otherwise.
routes:
  - app: gitlab

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: goma-gateway
  displayName: Goma Gateway
  version: 1.2.0
  description: Lightweight declarative API gateway and reverse proxy — routing, middleware, rate limiting, authentication and TLS.
  category: Web
  icon: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jkaninda/goma-gateway/main/logo.png
  homepage: https://jkaninda.github.io/goma-gateway
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    email: me@jkaninda.dev
    website: https://jkaninda.dev
  tags: [gateway, api-gateway, reverse-proxy, routing, middleware, tls]
  minMiabi: "1.8.1"

inputs:
  - key: log_level
    label: Log level
    help: Verbosity of the gateway log.
    type: select
    options: [debug, info, warn, error, off]
    default: info
  - key: enable_metrics
    label: Prometheus metrics
    help: Expose /metrics on the gateway. Put an auth middleware in front of it before routing that path publicly.
    type: bool
    default: "true"

volumes:
  # extra/ holds hot-reloaded routes and middlewares; certs/ holds certificates you bring yourself.
  - name: data    # /etc/goma
  - name: acme    # /etc/letsencrypt

configs:
  # Edit under Configs to redeploy; routes you want to change without a restart belong in /etc/goma/extra.
  - name: config
    mode: "0644"
    files:
      goma.yml: |
        version: "2"
        gateway:
          timeouts:
            read: 60
            write: 60
            idle: 60

          entryPoints:
            web:
              address: "[::]:8080"
            webSecure:
              address: "[::]:8443"

          monitoring:
            host: ''                                    # any host; set one to pin /healthz and /metrics to it
            enableMetrics: {{ .inputs.enable_metrics }}
            metricsPath: /metrics
            enableLiveness: true                        # /healthz — the app healthcheck depends on it
            enableReadiness: true                       # /readyz

          log:
            level: {{ .inputs.log_level }}

          # Drop YAML files here to add routes and middlewares without a redeploy; Goma watches the directory.
          extraConfig:
            directory: /etc/goma/extra
            watch: true

          # Empty: the gateway answers /healthz and 404s everything else until you add a route.
          routes: []

        middlewares: []

applications:
  - name: goma-gateway
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/goma-gateway
    tag: "1.2.0"
    ports:
      # Attach a Miabi domain to plain HTTP since TLS terminates at the platform gateway; 8443 is for direct traffic.
      - container: 8080
        scheme: http
      - container: 8443
        scheme: https
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /etc/goma
      - volume: acme
        path: /etc/letsencrypt
      # Lands inside the /etc/goma volume, at the path Goma loads by default.
      - config: config
        key: goma.yml
        path: /etc/goma/goma.yml
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /healthz
      port: 8080
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10

kind: Template
metadata:
  name: invoiceninja
  displayName: Invoice Ninja
  version: 1.2.0
  minMiabi: "1.10.10" # routes
  description: Self-hosted invoicing, quotes, payments and time tracking for freelancers and small businesses.
  category: Productivity
  icon: https://github.com/invoiceninja.png
  homepage: https://invoiceninja.com
  tags: [invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, crm]
inputs:
  - key: app_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL Invoice Ninja is served on. It ends up in invoice links, payment redirects and emails.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://invoices.example.com
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: Email of the account created on first start.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the initial account. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
  - key: app_key
    label: Application key
    help: Laravel encryption key. Leave blank to auto-generate — changing it later makes stored credentials unreadable.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
    required: true
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: mysql
    version: "8"
    placement: auto
  - name: redis
    engine: redis
    version: "8-alpine"
    placement: dedicated
volumes:
  # public holds web assets, storage uploads and PDFs; both are shared with nginx, which serves static files.
  - name: public
  - name: storage
applications:
  # The image is php-fpm only (port 9000), so the nginx sidecar below is the entry point.
  - name: app
    image: invoiceninja/invoiceninja-debian
    tag: "5.13.53"
    env:
      APP_URL: "{{ .inputs.app_url }}"
      APP_KEY: "base64:{{ base64 .inputs.app_key }}"
      APP_ENV: production
      APP_DEBUG: "false"
      # TLS terminates at the gateway; requiring HTTPS in the app too would redirect-loop.
      REQUIRE_HTTPS: "false"
      TRUSTED_PROXIES: "*"

      DB_CONNECTION: mysql
      DB_HOST: "{{ .databases.db.host }}"
      DB_PORT: "{{ .databases.db.port }}"
      DB_DATABASE: "{{ .databases.db.name }}"
      DB_USERNAME: "{{ .databases.db.user }}"
      DB_PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"

      CACHE_DRIVER: redis
      QUEUE_CONNECTION: redis
      SESSION_DRIVER: redis
      REDIS_HOST: "{{ .databases.redis.host }}"
      REDIS_PORT: "{{ .databases.redis.port }}"
      REDIS_PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.redis.password }}"

      # The account seeded on first start; the image skips this once one exists.
      IN_USER_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      IN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      FILESYSTEM_DISK: debian_docker
      PDF_GENERATOR: snappdf
      PHANTOMJS_PDF_GENERATION: "false"
      MAIL_MAILER: log
    secretEnv:
      - APP_KEY
      - DB_PASSWORD
      - REDIS_PASSWORD
      - IN_PASSWORD
    mounts:
      - volume: public
        path: /var/www/html/public
      - volume: storage
        path: /var/www/html/storage
    healthcheck:
      type: none
  - name: web
    primary: true
    image: nginx
    tag: "1.30-alpine"
    ports:
      - container: 80
        scheme: http
    # Config is in env because only env is interpolated and it must name the app's network alias.
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        printf '%s\n' "$NGINX_CONF" > /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
        until [ -f /var/www/html/public/index.php ]; do sleep 2; done
        exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'
    env:
      NGINX_CONF: |
        client_max_body_size 20M;

metadata:

  version: 1.1.0

  category: Security
  icon: https://github.com/lldap.png
  homepage: https://github.com/lldap/lldap
  author:
    name: LLDAP contributors
    website: https://github.com/lldap/lldap
  tags: [ldap, authentication, directory, users, groups, sso, self-hosted]
  minMiabi: "1.10.10" # routes

inputs:
  - key: base_dn
    label: Base DN
    help: 'The namespace for every user and group, conventionally your domain. You do not need to own it, but you cannot change it after the first start without recreating the directory — every app you connect will be configured with it.'
    type: string
    required: true
    default: dc=example,dc=com
    placeholder: dc=example,dc=com
    pattern: "^dc=[A-Za-z0-9-]+(,dc=[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*$"
  - key: http_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The URL the web interface is served on. It is used to build password-reset links, so it must be the URL a user's browser can reach.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://lldap.example.com
  - key: admin_username
    label: Admin username
    help: 'The first administrator. With the default "admin" and the base DN above, the LDAP bind DN becomes cn=admin,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com — the value other apps bind with.'
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin
    pattern: "^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,32}$"
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: Email for the admin account, used only when the account is first created.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the admin account, for both the LDAP bind and the web interface. Minimum 8 characters. Leave blank to auto-generate, then change it after signing in.
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 20
  - key: key_seed
    label: Key seed
    help: "Derives the private key that protects every stored password. Leave blank to auto-generate — then back it up somewhere other than this server: change it and every existing password stops working, since the hashes were computed against the key it derives."
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 32
  - key: jwt_secret
    label: JWT secret
    help: Signs web sessions. Leave blank to auto-generate; rotating it only signs everyone out.
    type: password
    required: true
    generate: true
    length: 32

# The volume is required even with Postgres: the entrypoint exits if /data is missing or unwritable.
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto

volumes:
  - name: data

applications:
  - name: lldap
    primary: true
    image: lldap/lldap
    tag: "v0.6.3"
    ports:
      # The web UI; LDAP listens on 3890 on the workspace network, see the README before exposing it.
      - container: 17170

    env:

      LLDAP_DATABASE_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}"

      LLDAP_LDAP_BASE_DN: "{{ .inputs.base_dn }}"
      LLDAP_LDAP_USER_DN: "{{ .inputs.admin_username }}"
      LLDAP_LDAP_USER_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      LLDAP_LDAP_USER_PASS: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      LLDAP_JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
      # An empty key_file stops LLDAP from also generating a key on disk next to the seed-derived one.
      LLDAP_KEY_FILE: ""

      LLDAP_LDAP_PORT: "3890"
      LLDAP_HTTP_PORT: "17170"
      LLDAP_VERBOSE: "false"
    secretEnv:
      - LLDAP_DATABASE_URL
      - LLDAP_LDAP_USER_PASS
      - LLDAP_KEY_SEED
      - LLDAP_JWT_SECRET
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /health
      port: 17170
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 15

routes:
  - app: lldap
    host: "{{ .inputs.http_url }}"

  minMiabi: "1.10.10"
  tags: [status-page, incidents, maintenance, uptime]
inputs:
  - key: dashboard_url
    label: Dashboard URL
    help: The public URL of the OpenStatus dashboard. Sign-in links are built from it, so it must be the address you open in the browser.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://status-admin.example.com
  - key: status_url
    label: Status page URL
    help: Optional. The public address of your status page; a route to it is created when its domain belongs to this workspace. Set the same host as the page's custom domain (see the README).
    type: string
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://status.example.com
  - key: auth_secret
    label: Auth secret
    help: Signs sessions. Leave blank to auto-generate; changing it later signs everyone out.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 44
    required: true
  - key: cron_secret
    label: Internal secret
    help: Required by OpenStatus at startup. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
    required: true
  - key: github_client_id
    label: GitHub OAuth client ID
    help: Optional. Adds "Sign in with GitHub". Without any provider, sign in with the magic link printed in the dashboard's logs.
    type: string
  - key: github_client_secret
    label: GitHub OAuth client secret
    type: password
  - key: oidc_issuer
    label: OIDC issuer URL
    help: Optional. Adds single sign-on through an OIDC provider such as authentik or Keycloak.
    type: string
    placeholder: https://auth.example.com/application/o/openstatus/
  - key: oidc_client_id
    label: OIDC client ID
    type: string
  - key: oidc_client_secret
    label: OIDC client secret
    type: password
  - key: oidc_name
    label: OIDC button label
    type: string
    default: SSO
  - key: resend_api_key
    label: Resend API key
    help: Optional, and rarely useful self-hosted. OpenStatus sends mail from its own openstatus.dev address, which Resend only accepts for that domain's owner. Sign-in does not need it.
    type: password
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: libsql
# The migration runner, dashboard and status page all use the same libSQL database.
stack:
  description: OpenStatus status pages — a dashboard, the public status page and their libSQL database.
  env:
    DATABASE_URL: "http://{{ .databases.db.host }}:{{ .databases.db.port }}"
    DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"
    NODE_ENV: production
    CRON_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.cron_secret }}"
  secretEnv:
    - DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN
    - CRON_SECRET
applications:
  # Runs migrations and exits; on-failure keeps a clean exit from restarting, and a redeploy runs it again.
  - name: migrate
    image: ghcr.io/openstatushq/openstatus-db-migrate
    tag: "4511a22"
    restartPolicy: on-failure
    healthcheck:
      type: none
  - name: dashboard
    primary: true
    image: ghcr.io/openstatushq/openstatus-dashboard
    tag: "4511a22"
    ports:
      - container: 3000
        scheme: http
    env:
      PORT: "3000"
      HOSTNAME: 0.0.0.0
      AUTH_TRUST_HOST: "true"
      # Self-host mode logs the sign-in magic link instead of emailing it.
      SELF_HOST: "true"
      NEXT_PUBLIC_URL: "{{ .inputs.dashboard_url }}"
      # Without it, sign-in links point at the container's own 0.0.0.0:3000.
      AUTH_URL: "{{ .inputs.dashboard_url }}"
      AUTH_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.auth_secret }}"
      AUTH_GITHUB_ID: "{{ .inputs.github_client_id }}"
      AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.github_client_secret }}"
      AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER: "{{ .inputs.oidc_issuer }}"
      AUTH_OIDC_ID: "{{ .inputs.oidc_client_id }}"
      AUTH_OIDC_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.oidc_client_secret }}"
      AUTH_OIDC_NAME: "{{ .inputs.oidc_name }}"
      # Validated as non-empty at startup even when no mail is sent.
      RESEND_API_KEY: '{{ default "disabled" .inputs.resend_api_key }}'
    secretEnv:
      - AUTH_SECRET
      - AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET
      - AUTH_OIDC_SECRET
      - RESEND_API_KEY
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /
      port: 3000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 10
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 60
  - name: status-page
    image: ghcr.io/openstatushq/openstatus-status-page
    tag: "4511a22"
    ports:
      - container: 3000
        scheme: http
    env:
      PORT: "3000"
      HOSTNAME: 0.0.0.0
      AUTH_TRUST_HOST: "true"
      SELF_HOST: "true"
      NEXT_PUBLIC_URL: "{{ .inputs.dashboard_url }}"
      AUTH_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.auth_secret }}"
      RESEND_API_KEY: '{{ default "disabled" .inputs.resend_api_key }}'
    secretEnv:
      - AUTH_SECRET
      - RESEND_API_KEY
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /
      port: 3000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 10
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 60
# Created on install when the URL's domain belongs to this workspace; skipped with a warning otherwise.

    host: "{{ .inputs.dashboard_url }}"
  - app: status-page
    host: "{{ .inputs.status_url }}"

  description: Posta — the API/web server and its dedicated worker, sharing one network and configuration.
  env:
    POSTA_ENV: production

    # Database (a managed PostgreSQL database, resolved by placement).
    POSTA_DB_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}?sslmode=disable"

    # Redis (a dedicated managed instance — Miabi sets a password on it).
    POSTA_REDIS_URL: "{{ .databases.redis.uri }}"
    
    POSTA_WEB_URL: "{{ .inputs.web_url }}"
    POSTA_CORS_ORIGINS: "{{ .inputs.web_url }}"
    # The worker needs both too: it signs outgoing mail (JWT secret) and decrypts stored SMTP passwords.
    POSTA_JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
    POSTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY: "{{ .inputs.encryption_key }}"
  secretEnv:
    # Both URLs embed their password, so they are stored encrypted like one.
    - POSTA_DB_URL
    - POSTA_REDIS_URL
    - POSTA_JWT_SECRET
    - POSTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY
volumes:
  - name: data
applications:
  - name: server
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/posta
    tag: "0.15.0"
    ports:
      - container: 9000
        scheme: http
    env:
      POSTA_ADMIN_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      POSTA_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      # Running jobs in-process too would double every delivery attempt.
      POSTA_EMBEDDED_WORKER: "false"

      # Email verification endpoint (results cached in Redis).
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_ENABLED: "true"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_CACHE_TTL_HOURS: "168"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_MX_CACHE_TTL_HOURS: "24"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_RATE_HOURLY: "1000"
      # Enables the public /api/v1/f/{key} form-ingest endpoint and the messages routes.
      POSTA_MESSAGES_ENABLED: "true"
      POSTA_MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_BYTES: "65536"
      POSTA_MESSAGES_MAX_ATTACH_SIZE: "5242880"
      # Per-IP submissions allowed per window (0 disables — leaves a public endpoint open to flooding)
      POSTA_MESSAGES_IP_RATE_LIMIT: "20"
      # Rate-limit window in seconds
      POSTA_MESSAGES_IP_RATE_WINDOW: "3600"
      # Per-form submissions allowed per hour
      POSTA_MESSAGES_PER_FORM_HOURLY: "200"
      # Per-sender-address submissions allowed per hour, per form
      POSTA_MESSAGES_PER_EMAIL_HOURLY: "5"
      # Per-workspace submissions allowed per day
      POSTA_MESSAGES_PER_WORKSPACE_DAILY: "1000"
    secretEnv:
      - POSTA_ADMIN_PASSWORD
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /healthz
      port: 9000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10

  # Same image with the `worker` command, so it scales independently of the API.
  - name: worker
    image: jkaninda/posta
    tag: "0.15.0"
    command: ["worker"]
    env:
      POSTA_WORKER_CONCURRENCY: "10"
      POSTA_WORKER_MAX_RETRIES: "5"
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: none

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: qdrant
  displayName: Qdrant
  version: 1.1.0
  description: Vector database for similarity search, embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation.
  category: Database
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/qdrant
  homepage: https://qdrant.tech
  tags: [database, vector, embeddings, search, ai]
inputs:
  - key: api_key
    label: API key
    help: Key clients must send in the api-key header. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
    required: true
volumes:
  - name: storage
applications:
  - name: qdrant
    primary: true
    image: qdrant/qdrant
    tag: "v1.20.0"
    # gRPC stays on 6334, reachable over the workspace network.
    ports:
      - container: 6333
        scheme: http
    env:
      QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY: "{{ .inputs.api_key }}"
    secretEnv:
      - QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY
    mounts:
      - volume: storage
        path: /qdrant/storage
    # The image ships neither curl nor wget, so the probe uses bash's /dev/tcp.
    healthcheck:
      type: command
      command: >-
        bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/6333 &&
        printf "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n" >&3 &&
        cat <&3 | grep -q passed'
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 15

    length: 24
    required: true
    pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._:@-]{8,}$'
volumes:
  - name: data
applications:
  - name: valkey
    primary: true
    image: valkey/valkey
    tag: "9-alpine"
    # The entrypoint appends $VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS; overriding the command would skip its drop-to-valkey-user step.
    env:
      VALKEY_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.password }}"
      VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS: "--requirepass {{ .inputs.password }} --appendonly yes"
    secretEnv:
      - VALKEY_PASSWORD
      - VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: command
      command: valkey-cli -a "$VALKEY_PASSWORD" --no-auth-warning ping | grep -q PONG
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10

  description: A tiny self-hosted guestbook — Okapi (Go) + Postgres with live SSE updates, an online-user count, and a server-time card. The reference example for deploying to Miabi.
  category: Development
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/go
  homepage: https://github.com/miabi-io/guestbook
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    website: https://github.com/jkaninda
    email: ''
  tags: [example, go, okapi, guestbook, sse]
inputs:
  - key: app_name
    label: Display name
    help: Shown in the guestbook header and health payload.
    type: string
    default: Miabi Guestbook
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto
applications:
  - name: guestbook
    primary: true
    image: miabi/guestbook
    tag: "1.0.0"
    ports:
      - container: 8080
        scheme: http
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}"
      APP_NAME: "{{ .inputs.app_name }}"
    secretEnv:
      - DATABASE_URL
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /healthz
      port: 8080

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: okapi-example
  displayName: Okapi Example
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Reference app for the Okapi Go API framework — middleware, routing, real-time SSE, and auto-generated OpenAPI docs at /docs.
  category: Development
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/go
  homepage: https://github.com/jkaninda/okapi-example
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    website: https://github.com/jkaninda
  tags: [api, go, okapi, example]
inputs:
  - key: jwt_secret
    label: JWT secret
    help: Used to sign tokens. Leave blank to auto-generate a strong secret.
    type: password
    generate: true
applications:
  - name: okapi-example
    image: jkaninda/okapi-example
    tag: latest
    ports:
      - container: 8080
        scheme: http
    env:
      JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
      ENABLE_DOCS: "true"
    secretEnv: [JWT_SECRET]
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /
      port: 8080
